_note: ONE folder level per type. This is the only taxonomy baked into the filesystem - everything else is tags. Because the category also lives in asset.json, changing this list later is a reorg command, not a weekend of dragging folders. Keep each list short: if you hesitate between two, it should be a tag instead.

rules._closed_vocabulary: The scanner may only assign a category from this list. New categories are added here deliberately, so the tree cannot sprawl on its own.

categories._texture_note: Seeded from the existing folder names in H:/3D/Maya/assets/texture, lightly singularised. Migration maps old folder -> category 1:1, so nothing has to be re-sorted by hand.
categories._texture_ground_note: 2026-10-14, for the Poly Haven port: one category per subcategory of their Ground & Terrain, flattened, because max_depth is 1 and a 'ground' level would break library/{type}/{category}/{asset}. Five are new (forest_floor, gravel, regolith, rocky_ground, sand); three already existed and are reused rather than duplicated - Soil & Mud is dirt, Grass & Vegetation is grass, Snow is snow. A 'soil' beside 'dirt' would be exactly the hesitation the note above says belongs in a tag. rocky_ground is NOT rock: Poly Haven files ground strewn with stones under Ground & Terrain and cliffs and boulders under Stone, and the two shade and tile differently.
categories._script_note: Sorted by the app that runs it, not by what it does - a tool is looked for where it can be loaded, and 'rigging' or 'export' say nothing about whether Houdini can open it. Function goes in tags.

_groups: 2026-10-14, Felix: a SIDEBAR heading over several categories, never a folder. Disk stays library/{type}/{category}/{asset}, three levels, always (architecture.md) - a fourth level would move every path builder, the index, verify, sync, the server and materialise to buy a heading. Clicking a group shows every category in it. A category belongs to at most one group; one listed here that is not in the type's categories is ignored.

suggested_tag_namespaces._note: Tags are free-form, but namespaced prefixes keep them searchable instead of turning into soup. The UI should offer these as autocomplete groups.
